subject: Architecture
title: Teotihuacán: The City of Gods
description: A quick, practical guide to Teotihuacán: The City of Gods.

hook.text: Teotihuacán was the largest city in the Americas in 100 AD — home to 125,000 people in planned neighborhoods.

buildup.text: The Avenue of the Dead runs two miles through the city, lined with platforms, temples, and pyramids.

discovery.text: The Pyramid of the Sun is the third-largest pyramid on Earth — built with three million tons of material.

twist.text: Nobody knows who built it. The Aztecs arrived 700 years later and named it — they were just as mystified.

climax.text: Recent tunnel excavations found mercury pools, jade figures, and seashells deep under the pyramids.

punchline.text: The city that dwarfed Rome. Built by people whose name we still don't know.

quiz.question: Who originally built Teotihuacán?
options: Unknown — the builders' identity remains a mystery
